text.tspan: TOWER
TRACKER
TASKS
INFO
Your reset day. Work through this list top to bottom — remove first, then prune,
then prep new pods. Checking off tasks as you go will track your progress.
0 COMPLETE
RESET
QUICK CHECKS — TAKES 5 MINUTES
Check Reservoir Water Level
Plants drink more water than nutrients — top up between feeding days
Top up with plain water if below the minimum line
Listen for the pump — should be running quietly and consistently
Confirm water is trickling down through all pods from the top
Check Nursery Tray Moisture
While you have seedlings germinating on the lid
Dark green & moist to touch = fine, leave it alone
Light green & dry = re-soak for 5 minutes, drain, replace lid
Look for sprouts — lettuce 3–7 days, herbs 5–14 days, flowers 5–21 days
Deadhead Flowers
Especially petunias and dianthus — prevents petals dropping into reservoir
Pinch spent blooms at the base of the flower stem as soon as petals fade
Check reservoir area for any fallen petals and remove them
Deadheading triggers new buds — the more you do it the more it flowers
CORE MAINTENANCE — RESET EACH WEEK
Harvest Leafy Greens
OUTER LEAF METHOD
Cut from the outside in — never touch the center growing crown
Cut at the base of outer leaf stems with sharp scissors — don't pull
Never take more than 1/3 of the plant in one session
Harvest before leaves press against LEDs or neighboring pods
Chives: cut the whole clump to 1–2 inches tall, regrows within a week
Prune Herbs
Keep them bushy and productive — neglect causes bolting and legginess
Basil: pinch any flower buds the moment they appear · cut to a node if overgrown
Mint: trim runners escaping into other pods · cut hard to 3–4 inches if overgrown
Rosemary: snip 1–2 inches from stem tips only, never into woody growth
Add Plant Food
WEEK 3+ ONLY
Leafy greens need nitrogen-forward formula at lighter EC than fruiting plants
New seedlings weeks 1–2: plain water only, zero nutrients
Week 3: half dose · Week 4+: full dose weekly
Target EC 1.0–1.6 · Target pH 5.5–6.5
Overfeeding signs: brown crispy leaf edges, white crust on rockwool — flush 1 week
Mildew Prevention Spray
ALTERNATE WEEKS
Rotate to prevent resistance — morning application only so leaves dry fully
Week A: Baking soda spray — 1 tsp baking soda + 1 tsp dish soap + 1 qt water
Week B: Neem oil spray — few drops neem + 1 tsp dish soap + 1 qt water, shake constantly
Spray both sides of all leaves · never spray a freshly pruned stressed plant
Inspect for Pests & Mildew
Catch problems early before they spread across pods
Check undersides of all leaves — that's where pests hide and lay eggs
White powdery patches = mildew · Silver streaks = thrips · Fine webbing = spider mites
Any affected leaves: bag and trash immediately, never compost
Check Hibiscus Stake & Tilt
If still in the tower — monitor lean and adjust support
If leaning: pack a small piece of damp sponge beside the rockwool cube to wedge it upright
A bamboo skewer or chopstick inserted alongside the stem acts as a stake
Tie loosely with a twist tie or soft plant tape — never tight against the stem
Best long-term fix: transplant to a pot in full sun outdoors (see General tab)
DEEPER MAINTENANCE — SCHEDULE A 30 MIN SESSION
Full Reservoir Drain & Clean
Prevents salt buildup, algae, and root rot bacteria accumulation
Drain completely — don't just top up
Wipe interior with a cloth, rinse thoroughly
Add a few ml of 3% H2O2 to fresh clean water on refill
Mix fresh nutrient dose into the clean water before replacing
Root Inspection
Do during reservoir drain when you can see roots clearly
Gently pull each pod slightly to check roots below
White & fuzzy = perfect · Tan/beige = normal · Brown & slimy = treat immediately
If brown & slimy: rinse, trim dead roots, soak in 1:5 H2O2 solution for 10 min
Triage Declining Pods
Regular turnover keeps the garden productive — don't hang onto lost causes
Remove any pod more than 50% brown or with slimy base
Clean empty pods with H2O2 solution, air dry fully
Start new yCubes in nursery tray to replace pulled pods
DEEP CLEAN SESSION — ABOUT AN HOUR
Root Trimming
Roots clogging the pump starve every plant in the system silently
Do during reservoir drain so roots are fully visible
Sterilize scissors with rubbing alcohol before starting
Trim only roots clogging the reservoir or wrapping the pump
Never remove more than 1/3 of root mass at once
Pump Clean
A failing pump can kill every plant within 24 hours
Remove pump, rinse under warm water
Clear any root debris or algae from the intake
Return and confirm strong water flow from the top of the tower
Tower Column Scrub
Algae and mineral deposits restrict water flow over time
Remove all pods, rinse column interior with warm water
Bottle brush for algae · 1:1 white vinegar soak 15 min for mineral deposits
Rinse thoroughly before replacing pods — vinegar residue affects pH
Tip: Tasks reset each session — uncheck everything at the start of a new maintenance day to use
this as a fresh checklist. Full guides and how-tos for every task are in the General Care Guide
tab.
